newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuelan stocks hit record on oil euphoria. [CORRECTED 21:40 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Venezuelan stocks hit record on oil euphoria. [CORRECTED 21:40 GMT]

text.p: Caracas stocks rose to a record high as euphoria spread to equities from on-going successes and strong bids in the second day of Venezuela's third round of oil contract auctions, traders said.
The bolsa's 19-share index vaulted 2.73 percent on foreign buying, busting through psychological resistance to end at 7,042.69 points, according to preliminary figures from the exchange.
Merinvest's composite index meanwhile rose 3.53 percent to close at 112.95 points.
"There's a lot of optimism, above all by foreigners, due to the success of the oil round," Union broker Hector Perez said.

Venezuela moved Tuesday into its second day of auctions with bids for oil field operating contracts exceeding expectations. The auctions continue through the week and are the third phase of state oil company PDVSA's strategy to increase production at mature oil fields.
"It's encouraging for investors who see potential in the country," Perez added.
In the stockmarket, 62 million shares traded worth 11 billion bolivars ($23 million). Telephone company CANTV led gainers, rising 6.4 percent to end at 2709.00 bolivars.

Despite the oil round's success, "be wary over over-heating on the IBC," warned New York based analysts IDEA who see 7,200 points as the bolsa's next target with profit-taking setting in next week after the attention-grabbing auctions end.
